Perhaps we should replace with JUnit 4 imports (org.junit.Test, org.junit.Before, etc.) and Mockito static imports. Simpler: Use JUnit 4 (since the environment may have JUnit 4). The code uses @Test from JUnit 4 already imported (org.junit.Test). But also uses JUnit Jupiter annotations like @BeforeEach, @ExtendWith, Assertions.*. We can replace them with JUnit 4 equivalents: @Before, @Test from org.junit.Test, and use org.junit.Assert.* static methods. Remove MockitoExtension and ExtendWith. Use Mockito directly.

Also remove duplicate imports. Use static import for org.junit.Assert.*.

Also need to import org.mockito.Mockito.* for mock, when, etc.

Simplify: Remove @ExtendWith annotation.

Change @BeforeEach to @Before.

Replace assertThrows with try-catch using JUnit 4's ExpectedException? JUnit 4 has assertThrows only in later versions (JUnit 4.13). Use import static org.junit.Assert.assertThrows; but JUnit 4's assertThrows signature: <T extends Throwable> T assertThrows(Class<T> expectedThrowable, Runnable executable). It doesn't have message param. So adjust.

Change assertEquals with message param: JUnit 4's assertEquals(String message, expected, actual). The order is message first. In code they used assertEquals(expected, actual, message). We'll swap.

Similarly assertNotEquals exists in JUnit 4.11? JUnit 4.11 introduced assertNotEquals? Actually assertNotEquals added in JUnit 4.11. signature: assertNotEquals(String message, expected, actual). We'll adjust.

Also assertThrows signature: assertThrows(Class<T>, Executable) where Executable is java.util.concurrent.Callable? Actually JUnit 4's assertThrows takes Class<T>, Runnable. We'll use lambda.

Let's rewrite test class.

Also need import org.junit.Before; import org.junit.Test; import static org.junit.Assert.*; import static org.mockito.Mockito.*;

Remove duplicate imports.

Also remove NaN import confusion: they import org.ta4j.core.num.NaN and static import NaN.NaN. Might be okay. Keep.
